sheet-64-1.description: The upper strip of sheet 64 of the 1921 New Jersey coast volume, covering the southern part of Avalon on Seven Mile Beach between 35th Street and 28th Street. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right, and reaches from a row of lots beyond 2nd Avenue across 2nd Avenue and 1st Avenue to the Atlantic Ocean, whose shore cuts through the beach-side blocks. 2nd Avenue is a 120 ft avenue carrying the single track of the W.J. & S.R.R., with the R.R. station and an open platform near 32nd Street. Development is light: most lots are vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, a hose house with a hose drying rack, a plumbing shop, a store, a boarding house, an insurance office, a cement block manufactory, the Peermont Church near 1st Avenue and 32nd Street, a tennis court, and a dwelling on piles at the beach end of 31st Street. Water pipes (4 and 6 in.) and hydrants are drawn in the streets. The upper right corner carries the town note: population 200, prevailing winds, two hose carts, and the water works built in 1898 with driven wells, a gasoline pumping engine and a 50,000 gallon stand pipe. A compass rose sits on the heavy line that separates this strip from the lower strip of the sheet.
notes: 2nd Avenue is today Dune Drive (a divided road in the old 120 ft right-of-way, which also held the railroad); 1st Avenue is today First Avenue.
The 2nd Avenue control points are the drawn centre of the avenue matched to the centre of the modern parcel right-of-way; the OpenStreetMap nodes lie on one carriageway, 5 to 8 m off the centre.
The beach has been built out since 1921: modern Avalon Avenue lies on what was then beach or ocean.

Printed sheet 64 (N.J.C.M. Vol. 4), Scale 100 ft to an inch, north towards the upper right (rotation about 56 deg). Two strips separated by a heavy line: part 1 above, 35th St to 28th St from the blocks beyond 2nd Av (W.J.& S.R.R. in 2nd Av, today Dune Drive) across 1st Av (today First Avenue) to the Atlantic Ocean; part 2 below, 28th St to 20th St, 2nd Av to the ocean. Water facilities and population note top right; R.R. station on 2nd Av; Peermont Church.

sheet-64-2.description: The lower strip of sheet 64 of the 1921 New Jersey coast volume, covering Avalon between 28th Street and 21st Street, with the edge of the block beyond 21st Street. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right and runs from 2nd Avenue, a 120 ft avenue with the W.J. & S.R.R. track down its middle, across 1st Avenue to the Atlantic Ocean, which reaches the ends of the blocks between 28th and 24th Streets. Nearly all the lots are vacant; a dozen frame dwellings stand in the blocks between 27th and 24th Streets and one near 22nd Street. Water pipes (4 and 6 in.) and hydrants are shown in the streets. The sheet scale bar, Scale 100 Ft. to One Inch, is printed in 1st Avenue near 22nd Street, and a note at the right edge gives 1850 ft to sheet No. 65. The top of the strip is the heavy line separating it from the upper strip, with a compass rose straddling it.
notes: 2nd Avenue is today Dune Drive; 1st Avenue is today First Avenue; 22nd and 21st Streets are West 22nd Street and West 21st Street in OpenStreetMap at these avenues.
21st Street / Dune Drive was not used: the modern right-of-way there is about 54 m wide.
The gap of 1850 ft to sheet 65 (about 20th to 14th Street) is not covered by this record.

Printed sheet 64 (N.J.C.M. Vol. 4), Scale 100 ft to an inch, north towards the upper right (rotation about 56 deg). Two strips separated by a heavy line: part 1 above, 35th St to 28th St from the blocks beyond 2nd Av (W.J.& S.R.R. in 2nd Av, today Dune Drive) across 1st Av (today First Avenue) to the Atlantic Ocean; part 2 below, 28th St to 20th St, 2nd Av to the ocean. Water facilities and population note top right; R.R. station on 2nd Av; Peermont Church.

sheet-65-1.description: The main map of sheet 65 of the 1921 New Jersey coast volume, covering the north end of Avalon between 12th Street and 4th Street, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right. It runs from 1st Avenue and Avalon Avenue on the ocean side across 2nd Avenue (120 ft) to 3rd Avenue and the blocks beyond it toward the bay; the upper left corner is taken by an inset box. The W.J. & S.R.R. (Pa. R.R.) crosses the large open block 8 between 9th and 8th Streets diagonally, with the depot, an R.R. house, a lumber shed and boat houses near the bay edge, and a note that the Leaming Hotel is 2100 ft along it (shown detached on this sheet). The Hotel Avalon occupies most of a block between 8th and 7th Streets south of 2nd Avenue; the Wells Memorial Presbyterian Church stands between 10th and 9th Streets, with bath houses, a paint shop, a hose house and hose cart, a post office, cement block buildings and many frame dwellings elsewhere. Beyond Avalon Avenue a row of lots is lettered K, J, I and H. The Atlantic Ocean shore crosses the lower right blocks between 6th and 4th Streets, where lots are drawn running into the water. Water pipes and hydrants are shown in the streets, and the scale bar is printed near Avalon Avenue.
notes: 2nd Avenue is today Dune Drive, 1st Avenue is First Avenue, 3rd Avenue keeps its name between 8th and 6th Streets (Ocean Drive further south); Avalon Avenue keeps its name.
North of about 6th Street the 1921 blocks (5th and 4th Streets and the beach blocks) are not in the modern street network; the shore here has changed.
Dune Drive control points use the parcel right-of-way centre, not the OpenStreetMap carriageway nodes.

Printed sheet 65 (N.J.C.M. Vol. 4), Scale 100 ft to an inch, north towards the upper right. Part 1: main map, 12th St to 4th St from beyond 3rd Av to Avalon Av, with the W.J.& S.R.R. diagonal and depot, Hotel Avalon, Wells Memorial Presbyterian Church, bath houses; ocean crosses the lower right blocks. Part 2: inset box at top left, 14th St to 12th St between 2nd Av and 1st Av (pumping station, public school). Part 3: detached strip at the top of the inset, Leaming Hotel and Leaming depot on Townsend's Inlet at 2nd St and 6th Av (2100 ft from 7th St along the railroad), drawn with north to the upper left; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: detached strip: Leaming Hotel and Leaming depot on Townsend's Inlet, 2nd St and 6th Av (no surviving street junction (2nd St is gone; the inlet shore and railroad have changed; no railroad in OpenStreetMap); needs hand-picked control from an aerial or a later edition showing the same buildings).

sheet-65-2.description: An inset in a heavy box at the upper left of sheet 65 of the 1921 New Jersey coast volume, showing the Avalon blocks between 14th Street and 12th Street from a row of lots beyond 2nd Avenue across 2nd Avenue to 1st Avenue. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the same orientation as the main map (north towards the upper right) and lies just west of the main map, which begins at 12th Street. 2nd Avenue is 120 ft wide with the W.J. & S.R.R. (Pa. R.R.) track. The block between 14th and 13th Streets holds the pumping station with an underground gasoline tank, a gasoline pumping engine and a water tank elevated 100 ft with a capacity of 50,000 gallons, the public school, a hen house and a few dwellings; the other blocks are almost empty. A note gives 1850 ft to sheet No. 64. Above the inset, separated by a heavy line, is a detached strip at Townsend's Inlet with the Leaming Hotel, which is not part of this inset.
notes: 2nd Avenue is today Dune Drive and 1st Avenue is First Avenue; 14th Street at First Avenue is West 14th Street in OpenStreetMap.
The detached strip above the inset (Leaming Hotel, Leaming depot, 2nd St and 6th Av at Townsend's Inlet) was not placed; see the sheet's unplaced list.
